verdict.rationale: Homebrew documents bulk operations as its own capability. `brew bundle` installs every dependency in a Brewfile with a single command, across formulae, casks, taps, VS Code extensions, npm, Cargo and more. It also starts listed services. `brew bundle dump` snapshots all installed packages into one file, and `brew bundle check || brew bundle install` is a scriptable state check. Further bulk commands are `brew untap` for one or more taps, autoremove of orphaned dependencies, and `brew upgrade --greedy` for all casks. Community reports confirm whole-system upgrades in practice: one user praised a fast `brew upgrade` session, and another complained it updates 'the entire world'. Missing for 10: documented filtered or pattern-based bulk actions (e.g. upgrade or uninstall a matched subset) and explicit docs for multi-item install/uninstall argument handling outside Brewfiles.
